title: Crude Oil Slides As Trump Offers More Time For Diplomacy To Resolve Iran Crisis
html:
Crude oil prices have moved lower on Friday as near-term war concerns eased after U.S. President Donald Trump stated that he prefers to give Iran more opportunity to strike a deal with the U.S. However, supply concerns due to incidents of ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi-Saudi Arabia conflict restricted the decline.

WTI Crude Oil for January delivery was last seen trading down by $0.67 (or 0.80%) at $83.01 per barrel.

November 27, 2026 15:08 ET The holiday-shortened week saw the release of some crucial indicators for the U.S. economy and some key appointments in the policy space in Europe. Growth and inflation data were in focus in the U.S. In Europe, the news of the selected nominee to replace the current ECB President Christine Lagarde made headlines. GDP data from Germany, the main economy in the region, also drew attention. In Asia, the South Korean central bank was in focus as it announced the latest interest rate decision.
